analysis.evidence: Abram is the subject of the opening verb. He went as YHWH had told him, and בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן identifies the journey as his departure from Haran.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: go, move from place to place

draft.change: Clear the unsupported root אבה and its link to article 2bh. Preserve the explanation of the compound name and its recorded bearer.
draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 identifies Abram as Terah’s son, and Genesis 17:5 records his change of name. The first element of אַבְרָם is the noun אָב, “father.” Neither verse supports deriving the name from אָבָה, “be willing.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אַבְרָם, “Abram went,” the name identifies the subject of וַיֵּלֶךְ. The verse goes on to give Abram’s age when he left Haran.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67605:30, 67344:6, 67337:9.
analysis.morphology: Relative particle with prefixed comparative preposition כַּ.
analysis.sense: with a preposition: as, where, than, until

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֵלָיו יַהְוֶה means “as Yahweh had spoken to him.” אֵלָיו identifies Abram as the addressee, and כַּאֲשֶׁר links his departure to Yahweh’s earlier instruction.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third person masculine singular, with יַהְוֶה as its subject.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אִתּוֹ לוֹט, אִתּוֹ means “with him” and refers to Abram. Lot went with Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.

evidence.note: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Terah’s genealogy names Lot as Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew. The passage gives no explanation of the name.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט with its etymology unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Lot as the son whom Haran fathered.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אִתּוֹ לוֹט, “Lot went with him,” לוֹט is the subject of וַיֵּלֶךְ. The pronoun in אִתּוֹ refers to Abram, whom Lot accompanies.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Haran’s son.

analysis.evidence: בֶּן introduces חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, five years plus seventy years, giving Abram’s age as seventy-five when he left Haran.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing the following expression of age.
